title: Find Sum of Array Product of Magical Sequences
summary: Given integers m, k, and an array nums, find the sum of the array products for all magical sequences of size m where each element is an index in nums, and the binary representation of the sum of powers of 2 corresponding to these indices has exactly k set bits.
statement: Given integers m, k, and an array nums, find the sum of the array products for all magical sequences of size m where each element is an index in nums, and the binary representation of the sum of powers of 2 corresponding to these indices has exactly k set bits. Return the result modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: 1 <= k <= m <= 30; nums has up to 50 positive values.
An ordered length-m index sequence is magical when the popcount of sum(2^index) equals k.
Sum the corresponding products of nums values modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Choosing how often each index occurs creates binary carries; the lowest carry bit is finalized before moving to the next index.
Memoize index, unassigned positions, remaining set bits, and carry, multiplying by combination counts and nums powers.
Try count occurrences, consume (carry+count)&1, shift the carry, and finish by checking its remaining popcount.
Every ordered sequence has one frequency allocation and one of comb(left,count) placements at each step, so the recurrence counts products with exact multiplicity.
editorial: Every ordered sequence has one frequency allocation and one of comb(left,count) placements at each step, so the recurrence counts products with exact multiplicity.

tests.explanation: The 120 permutations using each index once contribute products of 10^13, reduced modulo the modulus.
Exactly ordered pairs of distinct indices have two set bits; their products sum to 170.
